syllabus.Course Title: HISTORY OF COURTS, LEGISLATURES AND LEGAL PROFESSION IN INDIA

Course Content.UNIT I: Evolution of Courts in India: Administration of Justice in Presidency Towns (1600–1773); Judicial institutions under East India Company; Warren Hastings’ Plan of 1772; Adalat System; Reforms under Plan of 1774 and 1780; Regulating Act, 1773; Supreme Court at Calcutta; Act of 1781; Judicial Measures of Cornwallis; Adalat System under Sir John Shore
Course Content.UNIT V: Legal Profession in India: Legal Profession in Pre-British India; Ancient Indian legal system; Mayor’s Courts under Charter of 1726; Legal profession under Charter of 1774; Legal Practitioners Act, 1853; Enrolment of Advocates, Vakils and Attorneys; Advocates Act, 1961; Regulation of Legal Profession in India

Course Content.UNIT IV: Legislative Councils and Constitutional Reforms: Indian Councils Act, 1861; Central Legislative Council; Government of India Act, 1909; Government of India Act, 1919; Bicameral Legislature; Government of India Act, 1935; Federal Assembly and Council of States; Provincial Legislatures; Law Reform and Law Commission
Course Content.UNIT III: Development of Legislature: Legislative authority under Charter of 1600; Regulating Act, 1773; Act of 1781; Charter Act of 1813; Charter Act of 1833; Establishment of All India Legislature

syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the evolution of courts and judicial administration in British India. CO2: Analyze the development of High Courts and constitutional principles in India. CO3: Examine the growth of legislative institutions under British administration. CO4: Evaluate the constitutional and legal reforms introduced during colonial rule. CO5: Explain the historical evolution and regulation of the legal profession in India.

syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the principles and concepts underlying the Law of Evidence. CO2: Analyze rules governing relevancy, admissibility and evidentiary value of facts and statements. CO3: Examine legal provisions relating to admissions, confessions and documentary evidence. CO4: Apply evidentiary principles relating to burden of proof, witness examination and presumptions. CO5: Evaluate evidentiary rules in light of technological developments and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

msData.name: CIVIL PROCEDURE CODE AND LAW OF LIMITATION

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Civil Procedure Code: Codification of Civil Procedure; Introduction to CPC; Principal Features of CPC; Suits; Parties to Suit; Framing of Suit; Institution of Suits; Bars to Suit; Doctrine of Sub Judice; Doctrine of Res Judicata; Place of Suing; Transfer of Suits; Territorial Jurisdiction; Cause of Action; Jurisdictional Bars; Summons; Service of Foreign Summons
Course Content.UNIT V: Law of Limitation: Concept of Limitation; Object of Limitation Law; General Principles of Limitation; Extension of Limitation; Condonation of Delay; Sufficient Cause; Computation of Limitation; Acknowledgment; Part Payment; Legal Disability; Limitation Act, 1963 (excluding Schedule)
Course Content.UNIT II: Pleadings and Framing of Issues: Pleadings; Contents of Pleadings; Forms of Pleading; Striking out of Pleadings; Amendment of Pleadings; Plaint; Essentials of Plaint; Return of Plaint; Rejection of Plaint; Production and Marking of Documents; Written Statement; Counter Claim; Set Off; Application of Section 89 CPC; Framing of Issues
Course Content.UNIT IV: Special Suits and Appeals: Suits in Particular Cases; Suits by or against Government; Suits relating to Public Matters; Suits by or against Minors; Suits involving Persons of Unsound Mind; Suits by Indigent Persons; Interpleader Suits; Incidental Proceedings; Supplementary Proceedings. Appeals and Revisional Jurisdiction: Appeals; Reference; Review; Revision; Appeals from Original Decrees; Appeals from Appellate Decrees; Appeals from Orders; General Provisions relating to Appeals
Course Content.UNIT III: Trial, Judgment and Execution: Appearance and Examination of Parties; Adjournments; Ex Parte Procedure; Summoning and Attendance of Witnesses; Examination of Witnesses; Admissions; Production and Impounding of Documents; Return of Documents; Hearing; Affidavit; Judgment; Decree; Interim Orders and Stay; Injunctions; Appointment of Receivers; Appointment of Commissions; Costs. Execution Proceedings: Concept of Execution; General Principles of Execution; Powers of Executing Courts; Procedure for Execution; Modes of Execution; Arrest and Detention; Attachment and Sale

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the structure, principles and procedural framework of the Civil Procedure Code and Limitation Law. CO2: To explain institution of suits, pleadings, jurisdiction and procedural requirements in civil litigation. CO3: To develop understanding of execution proceedings, appeals and special civil proceedings. CO4: To analyze procedural remedies, interim orders and judicial mechanisms under CPC. CO5: To familiarize students with limitation principles, condonation of delay and computation of limitation periods.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Mulla – Code of Civil Procedure; C.K. Takwani – Civil Procedure; Sarkar – Civil Court Practice and Procedure; B.B. Mitra – Limitation Act; Sanjiva Row – Limitation Act; Sanjiva Row – Code of Civil Procedure; AIR Commentaries on Limitation Act – W.W. Chitaley; Bare Act – Code of Civil Procedure, 1908; Bare Act – Limitation Act, 1963; Justice C.K. Thakker – Code of Civil Procedure Commentary
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Satyadhyan Ghosal v Deorajin Debi; K.K. Velusamy v N. Palanisamy; Salem Advocate Bar Association v Union of India; T. Arivandandam v T.V. Satyapal; Ghanshyam Dass v Dominion of India; State of Punjab v Shamlal Murari; Collector Land Acquisition v Mst Katiji; Sangram Singh v Election Tribunal; A.V. Papayya Sastry v Government of Andhra Pradesh; Morgan Stanley Mutual Fund v Kartick Das
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the structure and procedural framework of the Civil Procedure Code and Limitation Act. CO2: Analyze legal principles relating to institution of suits, pleadings and jurisdiction. CO3: Examine execution proceedings, appeals and procedural remedies under CPC. CO4: Apply procedural rules relating to pleadings, injunctions, decrees and limitation in civil litigation. CO5: Evaluate procedural justice mechanisms and limitation principles in civil adjudication.

msData.name: LAW OF TORTS INCLUDING MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENTS AND CONSUMER PROTECTION LAWS

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Law of Torts: Nature of Law of Torts; Definition of Tort; Elements of Tort; Development of Law of Torts in England and India; Wrongful Act and Legal Damage; Damnum Sine Injuria; Injuria Sine Damno; Tort distinguished from Crime; Tort distinguished from Breach of Contract; General Principles of Liability in Torts; Fault; Wrongful Intent; Malice; Negligence; Liability without Fault; Statutory Liability; Parties to Proceedings
Course Content.UNIT V: Consumer Protection Laws: Common Law and Consumer Protection; Duty to Take Care; Liability for Negligence; Product Liability; Consumerism; Consumer Protection Act, 1986; Salient Features of Consumer Protection Act; Definition of Consumer; Rights of Consumers; Defects in Goods; Deficiency in Services; Unfair Trade Practices; Consumer Redressal Machinery; Liability of Service Providers; Liability of Manufacturers and Traders; Remedies under Consumer Protection Law
Course Content.UNIT II: General Defences and Liability Principles: General Defences to Tortious Liability; Vicarious Liability; Liability of State for Torts; Sovereign Immunity; Joint Liability; Liability of Joint Tortfeasors; Rule of Strict Liability; Rylands v Fletcher Rule; Rule of Absolute Liability; M.C. Mehta v Union of India Principle; Occupier’s Liability; Extinction of Liability; Waiver and Acquiescence; Release; Accord and Satisfaction; Death and Tortious Liability
Course Content.UNIT IV: Defamation, Negligence and Remedies: Defamation; Negligence; Torts against Business Relations; Injurious Falsehood; Negligent Misstatement; Passing Off; Conspiracy; Torts affecting Family Relations; Judicial Remedies; Extra-Judicial Remedies; Damages; Kinds of Damages; Assessment of Damages; Remoteness of Damage; Injunctions; Action Personalis Moritur Cum Persona
Course Content.UNIT III: Specific Torts and Motor Vehicle Liability: Torts Affecting Person: Assault; Battery; False Imprisonment; Malicious Prosecution; Nervous Shock. Torts Affecting Immovable Property: Trespass to Land; Public Nuisance; Private Nuisance. Torts Affecting Movable Property. Liability arising out of Accidents; Relevant Provisions of Motor Vehicles Act

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the nature, principles and development of Law of Torts. CO2: To examine general principles of tortious liability and defenses available under tort law. CO3: To analyze specific torts affecting person, property, business and family relations. CO4: To understand liability arising from motor vehicle accidents and remedies under tort law. CO5: To familiarize students with consumer protection laws, consumer rights and redressal mechanisms in India.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Winfield & Jolowicz – Law of Tort; Salmond & Heuston – Law of Torts; Ramaswamy Iyer – Law of Torts; PSA Pillai – Law of Tort; Durga Das Basu – Law of Torts; Ratanlal & Dhirajlal – Law of Torts; R.K. Bangia – Law of Torts; Vivienne Harpwood – Law of Torts; Hepple & Mathews – Tort: Cases and Materials; D.N. Saraf – Law of Consumer Protection in India; G.B. Reddy – Law of Consumer Protection in India
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Donoghue v Stevenson; Rylands v Fletcher; M.C. Mehta v Union of India; Ashby v White; Bhim Singh v State of Jammu and Kashmir; Lucknow Development Authority v M.K. Gupta; Indian Medical Association v V.P. Shantha; State of Rajasthan v Vidyawati; Municipal Corporation of Delhi v Subhagwanti; Kasturi Lal v State of Uttar Pradesh
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the nature, development and principles of Law of Torts and consumer protection laws. CO2: Analyze tortious liability, defenses and principles governing civil wrongs. CO3: Examine specific torts relating to person, property, negligence and business relations. CO4: Apply legal principles relating to motor vehicle accident liability and consumer disputes. CO5: Evaluate remedies available under tort law and consumer protection framework in India.

Course Content.UNIT I: Indemnity, Guarantee, Bailment and Pledge: Contract of Indemnity: Definition of Indemnity; Rights of Indemnity Holder; Liability of Indemnifier. Contract of Guarantee: Definition of Guarantee; Essentials of Contract of Guarantee; Distinction between Indemnity and Guarantee; Kinds of Guarantee; Rights and Liabilities of Surety; Discharge of Surety. Contract of Bailment: Definition of Bailment; Essentials of Bailment; Kinds of Bailment; Rights and Duties of Bailor and Bailee; Termination of Bailment. Pledge: Definition of Pledge; Rights and Duties of Pawnor and Pawnee; Pledge by Non-owner
Course Content.UNIT V: Partnership Law and LLP: Definition and Nature of Partnership; Formation of Partnership; Test of Partnership; Partnership and Other Associations; Registration of Firm; Effect of Non-registration; Relations of Partners; Rights and Duties of Partners; Property of Firm; Relation of Partners to Third Parties; Implied Authority of Partners; Kinds of Partners; Minor as Partner; Reconstitution of Firm; Dissolution of Firm; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)
Course Content.UNIT II: Contract of Agency: Definition of Agent; Creation of Agency; Rights and Duties of Agent; Delegation of Authority; Personal Liability of Agent; Relations between Principal and Agent with Third Parties; Termination of Agency
Course Content.UNIT IV: Transfer of Property and Rights of Parties: Property and Possession; Passing of Property; Sale by Non-owner; Nemo Dat Quod Non Habet; Delivery of Goods; Rights and Duties of Seller and Buyer; Rights of Unpaid Seller; Remedies for Breach of Contract
Course Content.UNIT III: Sale of Goods: Contract of Sale of Goods; Formation of Contract; Subject Matter of Sale; Conditions and Warranties; Express Conditions and Warranties; Implied Conditions and Warranties; Pricing; Doctrine of Caveat Emptor; Hire Purchase Agreements

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to special contracts under Indian Contract Act and related commercial laws. CO2: To examine legal principles relating to indemnity, guarantee, bailment, pledge and agency. CO3: To analyze contractual rights and liabilities arising under Sale of Goods law. CO4: To understand legal principles governing partnership firms and LLPs. CO5: To familiarize students with commercial transactions, contractual obligations and remedies under mercantile law.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Anson – Law of Contract; Venkatesh Iyyer – Law of Contracts and Tenders; Cheshire & Fifoot – Law of Contract; Mulla – Indian Contract Act; G.C.V. Subba Rao – Law of Contracts; Krishnan Nair – Law of Contracts; Avtar Singh – Law of Contracts; A. Ramaiah – Sale of Goods Act; Benjamin – Sale of Goods; P.S. Atiyah – Sale of Goods Act; Charles D. Drake – Law of Partnership; Bowstead – Law of Agency
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Hadley v Baxendale; Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co; Bolton v Mahadeva; State Bank of India v Indexport Registered; Lallan Prasad v Rahmat Ali; Pannalal Jankidas v Mohanlal; Bhopal Sugar Industries Ltd v Sales Tax Officer; Mohori Bibee v Dharmodas Ghose; Cox v Hickman; Kalyani Breweries Ltd v State of West Bengal
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts and legal principles governing special contracts under commercial law. CO2: Analyze rights, duties and liabilities arising under contracts of indemnity, guarantee, bailment and agency. CO3: Examine legal provisions relating to sale of goods and transfer of property in commercial transactions. CO4: Apply principles relating to agency, partnership and commercial contracts in practical situations. CO5: Evaluate contractual rights, liabilities and remedies arising from mercantile transactions and partnership relations.

Course Content.UNIT I: Environmental Studies and Biodiversity: Environmental Studies: Introduction to Environmental Studies; Definition, Scope and Importance; Basic Principles of Ecosystem Functioning; Concept of Ecosystem; Structure and Functions of Ecosystem; Different Ecosystems and their Features. Biodiversity and Conservation: Introduction to Biodiversity; Bio-Geographical Classification of India; Value of Biodiversity; Consumptive and Productive Use; Social, Ethical and Optional Values; Biodiversity at Global, National and Local Levels; Biodiversity Hotspots; Threats to Biodiversity; Endangered and Endemic Species of India; Conservation of Biodiversity; In-situ Conservation; Ex-situ Conservation
Course Content.UNIT V: Environmental Ethics and Sustainable Development: Social Issues and Environment: Sustainable Development; Resettlement and Rehabilitation; Environmental Problems and Concerns. Environmental Ethics: Environmental Ethics and Issues; Consumerism and Waste Products; Public Awareness; Sustainable Resource Management. Environmental Policy: Design of Environmental Policy; Government Regulation; Command and Control Mechanism
Course Content.UNIT II: Natural Resources and Environmental Economics: Environmental and Natural Resources: Forest Resources; Deforestation; Timber Extraction; Mining and Dams; Impact on Forests and Tribal Communities; Water Resources; Surface and Ground Water Utilization; Floods and Droughts; Water Conflicts; Food Resources; Agricultural Problems; Fertilizer and Pesticide Problems; Water Logging and Salinity. Environmental Valuation: Welfare Measures and Environmental Values; Classification of Environmental Values; Valuation Methods. Environmental Economics: Economic Approaches to Environmental Preservation; Conservation of Environment; Property Rights and Externalities; Management of Natural Resources
Course Content.UNIT IV: Environment, Development and Sustainability: Regional and Sectoral Issues: Urbanization; Agro-Forestry; Dry Lands; Goods and Services; Mountain Development; River Basin Water Resource Management; Sustainable Tourism; Coastal Zone Management. Environment and Development: Economy and Environment Interaction; State of Environment; Economics of Development; Preservation and Conservation. Sustainability: Theory and Practice of Sustainability; Equitable Use of Resources; Sustainable Lifestyles; Role of Individuals in Prevention of Pollution. Human Population and Environment: Population Growth and Environment; Human Rights and Environment
Course Content.UNIT III: Environmental Pollution and Problems in India: Environmental Pollution: Air Pollution; Water Pollution; Soil Pollution; Marine Pollution; Noise Pollution; Causes, Effects and Control Measures. Environmental Problems in India: Effects of Human Activities on Environment; Water and River Problems; Ground Water Issues; Wasteland Reclamation

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the concepts, scope and significance of environmental studies and ecosystem functioning. CO2: To examine environmental resources, biodiversity conservation and sustainable utilization of natural resources. CO3: To analyze environmental pollution, environmental economics and environmental management systems. CO4: To understand environmental sustainability, development issues and human interaction with the environment. CO5: To familiarize students with environmental ethics, public awareness and policy measures for environmental protection.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: B. Sudhakara Reddy – Environmental Studies; C. Manohar Chary & P. Jayaram Reddy – Principles of Environmental Studies; Y. Anjaneyulu – Introduction to Environmental Science; P.D. Sharma – Ecology and Environment; A.P. Rao & Ch. Rajaiah – Paryavaran Shastram; Erach Bharucha – Textbook of Environmental Studies; Shyam Divan & Armin Rosencranz – Environmental Law and Policy in India
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts, scope and importance of environmental studies and ecosystems. CO2: Analyze biodiversity, natural resources and environmental conservation methods. CO3: Examine causes, effects and control measures relating to environmental pollution and degradation. CO4: Apply principles of sustainability and environmental management to contemporary environmental issues. CO5: Evaluate environmental policies, ethics and sustainable development practices for environmental protection.
syllabus.Suggested Environmental Case, Laws: M.C. Mehta v Union of India; Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India; Subhash Kumar v State of Bihar; Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India; Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra v State of Uttar Pradesh; Narmada Bachao Andolan v Union of India; M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath; T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v Union of India; A.P. Pollution Control Board v Prof. M.V. Nayudu; Sterlite Industries v Union of India

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Criminal Law: Concept of Crime; Meaning of Crime; Distinction between Crime and Tort; Stages of Crime; Intention; Preparation; Attempt; Commission of Crime; Elements of Crime; Actus Reus; Mens Rea; Codification of Criminal Law in India; Indian Penal Code, 1860; Application of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023; Sections 1–2 of BNS, 2023; Territorial Application; Extra-Territorial Application; Definitions under BNS
Course Content.UNIT V: Offences Affecting Human Body: Hurt: Simple Hurt; Grievous Hurt; Sections 114–125 of BNS, 2023. Wrongful Restraint and Confinement: Sections 126–127 of BNS, 2023. Criminal Force and Assault: Sections 128–136 of BNS, 2023. Kidnapping, Abduction and Forced Labour: Sections 137–146 of BNS, 2023; Slavery; Forced Labour
Course Content.UNIT II: General Principles of Criminal Liability: General Explanations under Section 3 of BNS, 2023; Joint Liability; Group Liability; Individual Liability; Constructive Liability; Punishments under Sections 4–13 of BNS, 2023; Theories of Punishment; General Exceptions under Sections 14–44 of BNS, 2023; Abetment; Criminal Conspiracy; Attempt; Sections 45–62 of BNS, 2023
Course Content.UNIT IV: Offences Affecting Human Life: Offences affecting Human Life under Sections 100–110 of BNS, 2023; Culpable Homicide; Murder; Punishment for Life Convict; Causing Death by Negligence; Organized Crime under Section 111 of BNS, 2023; Petty Organized Crime under Section 112 of BNS, 2023; Terrorist Acts under Section 113 of BNS, 2023
Course Content.UNIT III: Offences against Women and Children: Sexual Offences: Sexual Offences under Sections 63–73 of BNS, 2023; Criminal Force and Assault against Women: Sections 74–79 of BNS, 2023; Offences relating to Marriage: Sections 80–86 of BNS, 2023; Kidnapping and Abduction: Section 87 of BNS, 2023; Causing Miscarriage: Sections 88–92 of BNS, 2023; Offences against Children: Sections 93–99 of BNS, 2023

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the concepts, principles and foundations of criminal law under BNS, 2023. CO2: To examine general principles of criminal liability, punishments and general exceptions under criminal law. CO3: To analyze offences relating to women, children and offences affecting human life under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. CO4: To understand offences affecting the human body and criminal responsibility under BNS, 2023. CO5: To familiarize students with comparative developments between IPC, 1860 and BNS, 2023 through judicial interpretation and contemporary criminal jurisprudence.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 – Bare Act; Ratan Lal & Dhiraj Lal – Indian Penal Code; Achutan Pillai – Criminal Law; Gour K.D. – Criminal Law: Cases and Materials; Kenny’s – Outlines of Criminal Law; O.P. Srivastava – General Principles of Criminal Law; K.D. Gaur – Textbook on Indian Penal Code; PSA Pillai – Criminal Law; Russell on Crime; Smith & Hogan – Criminal Law
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: K.M. Nanavati v State of Maharashtra; Bachan Singh v State of Punjab; State of Maharashtra v Mayer Hans George; Virsa Singh v State of Punjab; State of Rajasthan v Kashi Ram; Tukaram v State of Maharashtra; Mukesh v State (NCT of Delhi); Om Prakash v State of Uttar Pradesh; Shreya Singhal v Union of India; Maneka Gandhi v Union of India
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts, principles and evolution of criminal law under BNS, 2023. CO2: Analyze criminal liability, punishments, general exceptions and stages of crime under criminal law. CO3: Examine offences relating to women, children and offences affecting human life under BNS, 2023. CO4: Apply principles of criminal law to offences affecting the human body and public safety. CO5: Evaluate contemporary criminal justice developments and comparative changes between IPC, 1860 and BNS, 2023.

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Company Law: Corporate Personality; General Principles of Company Law; Nature and Definition of Company; Private Company; Public Company; Characteristics of Company; Kinds of Companies; Registration and Incorporation of Company; Lifting of Corporate Veil; Company distinguished from Partnership; Company distinguished from HUF; Company distinguished from LLP; Position under Companies Act, 1956 and Companies Act, 2013
Course Content.UNIT V: Corporate Restructuring and Winding Up: Accounts and Audit; Inspection and Investigation; Compromises; Reconstruction; Amalgamation; Majority Rule; Rights of Minority Shareholders; Prevention of Oppression and Mismanagement; Revival and Rehabilitation of Sick Companies; Mergers and Takeovers; Dissolution of Company; Winding Up of Companies; Modes of Winding Up; Consequences of Winding Up; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016; Authorities under Company Law; Department of Company Affairs; National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT); National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT); Registrar of Companies (ROC); Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO); Jurisdiction of Courts; Impact of Companies Act, 2013
Course Content.UNIT II: Promoters and Corporate Documents: Promoters; Memorandum of Association; Doctrine of Ultra Vires; Articles of Association; Doctrine of Indoor Management; Prospectus; Civil Liability for Misstatement in Prospectus; Criminal Liability for Misstatement in Prospectus; Statement in lieu of Prospectus; Pre-incorporation Contracts; Membership in Company; Borrowing Powers; Debentures; Charges; Position under Companies Act, 1956 and Companies Act, 2013
Course Content.UNIT IV: Directors and Meetings: Directors: Kinds of Directors; Appointment of Directors; Qualifications and Disqualifications; Powers of Directors; Rights and Duties of Directors. Meetings: Kinds of Meetings; Statutory Meeting; Statutory Report; Annual General Meeting; Extraordinary General Meeting; Tribunal’s Power to Order Meeting; Class Meetings; Essentials of Valid Meeting; Chairman of Meeting; Duties of Chairman; Proxy; Resolutions; Minutes. Corporate Governance: Shareholder Activism; Corporate Social Responsibility; Position under Companies Act, 1956 and Companies Act, 2013
Course Content.UNIT III: Shares and Share Capital: Shares and Stock; Kinds of Shares; Restrictions on Allotment of Shares; Intermediaries; Calls on Shares; Forfeiture of Shares; Transfer of Shares; Transmission of Shares; Rectification of Register; Share Certificates; Certification of Transfer of Shares; Limitation Period for Issue of Certificates; Effect of Share Certificate; Position under Companies Act, 1956 and Companies Act, 2013

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the concepts, principles and development of company law in India. CO2: To examine incorporation, management and functioning of companies under the Companies Act, 2013. CO3: To analyze legal principles relating to shares, directors, meetings and corporate governance. CO4: To understand corporate restructuring, winding up and protection of minority shareholders. CO5: To familiarize students with contemporary developments in corporate law and regulatory authorities under company law.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Shah – Lectures on Company Law; Avtar Singh – Company Law; Charlesworth – Company Law; Ramaiya – Company Law; Dutta – Company Law; Companies Act, 2013; Executive Programme Study Material on Company Law – ICSI; Gower – Principles of Modern Company Law; Palmer’s Company Law; Taxmann – Company Law and Practice
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Salomon v Salomon & Co Ltd; Lee v Lee's Air Farming Ltd; Foss v Harbottle; Ashbury Railway Carriage and Iron Co Ltd v Riche; Royal British Bank v Turquand; Daimler Co Ltd v Continental Tyre and Rubber Co; New Horizons Ltd v Union of India; LIC of India v Escorts Ltd; Needle Industries India Ltd v Needle Industries Newey India Holding Ltd; Tata Consultancy Services v Cyrus Investments Pvt Ltd
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts, characteristics and legal framework governing companies under company law. CO2: Analyze incorporation procedures, corporate documents and management structure of companies. CO3: Examine legal provisions relating to shares, directors, meetings and shareholder rights. CO4: Apply principles relating to corporate management, restructuring and winding up of companies. CO5: Evaluate corporate governance practices and regulatory mechanisms under the Companies Act, 2013.

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Environmental Law: Meaning and Definition of Environment; Ecology; Ecosystems; Biosphere; Biomes; Ozone Depletion; Global Warming; Climatic Changes; Preservation and Conservation of Environment; Ancient Indian Approach to Environment; Environmental Degradation; Environmental Pollution; Kinds of Pollution; Causes and Effects of Pollution
Course Content.UNIT V: International Environmental Law: International Environmental Regime; Transboundary Pollution; State Liability; Customary International Law; Liability of Multinational Corporations; Stockholm Declaration, 1972; Role of UNEP; Ramsar Convention, 1971; Bonn Convention, 1992; Nairobi Convention, 1982; Convention on Biological Diversity, 1992; Kyoto Protocol, 1997; Johannesburg Convention, 2002; UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC); COP21 and Paris Agreement, 2016
Course Content.UNIT II: Remedies against Environmental Pollution: Common Law Remedies against Pollution; Trespass; Negligence; Rule of Strict Liability; Rule of Absolute Liability; Relevant Provisions of IPC relating to Pollution; Relevant Provisions of Cr.P.C. relating to Public Nuisance; Relevant Provisions of C.P.C. relating to Public Nuisance; Remedies under Specific Relief Act; Relief against Smoke and Noise; Noise Pollution
Course Content.UNIT IV: Constitutional and Judicial Dimensions of Environmental Law: Article 48A of the Constitution; Article 51A(g) of the Constitution; Right to Wholesome Environment; Right to Development; Restriction on Trade and Occupation for Environmental Protection; Immunity under Article 31C; Legislative Powers of Centre and States; Writ Jurisdiction in Environmental Matters; Role of Indian Judiciary in Environmental Jurisprudence; Green Belt Development; Purpose and Advantages of Green Belts
Course Content.UNIT III: Environmental Protection Laws: Preservation and Conservation of Forests; Protection of Wildlife; Protection of Endangered Species; Protection of Marine Life; Coastal Ecosystems and Lakes; Prevention of Cruelty to Animals; Prevention and Control of Water Pollution; Air Pollution Control; Environmental Pollution Control Mechanisms; Environment Protection Act, 1986; Biological Diversity Act, 2002; Hazardous Waste Management and Handling Regulations; National Environment Tribunal; National Environmental Appellate Authority; National Green Tribunal (NGT); Powers and Jurisdiction of NGT

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the concepts, principles and significance of environmental law and environmental protection. CO2: To examine common law remedies and statutory mechanisms relating to environmental pollution and environmental justice. CO3: To analyze laws relating to forests, wildlife, biodiversity and pollution control in India. CO4: To understand constitutional provisions and judicial approaches relating to environmental protection and sustainable development. CO5: To familiarize students with international environmental law, global environmental conventions and environmental governance mechanisms.

Agarwal – Legal Control of Environmental Pollution; Chetan Singh Mehta – Environmental Protection and Law; V.K. Leelakrishnan – Environmental Law in India; Shyam Divan & Armin Rosencranz – Environmental Law and Policy in India; Environmental Protection Act, 1986
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: M.C. Mehta v Union of India; Vellore Citizens Welfare Forum v Union of India; Indian Council for Enviro-Legal Action v Union of India; Subhash Kumar v State of Bihar; M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath; T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v Union of India; Rural Litigation and Entitlement Kendra v State of Uttar Pradesh; A.P. Pollution Control Board v Prof. M.V. Nayudu; Narmada Bachao Andolan v Union of India; Sterlite Industries v Union of India
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts, principles and significance of environmental law and environmental protection. CO2: Analyze environmental pollution, liability principles and remedies available under environmental law. CO3: Examine statutory and constitutional mechanisms for preservation and conservation of the environment. CO4: Apply environmental law principles and judicial precedents to environmental disputes and policy issues. CO5: Evaluate international environmental regimes, sustainable development policies and contemporary environmental challenges.

Course Content.UNIT I: Offences against State and Elections: Offences against State; Sections 147–158 of BNS, 2023; Offences relating to Army, Navy and Air Force; Sections 159–168 of BNS, 2023; Offences relating to Elections; Sections 169–177 of BNS, 2023
Course Content.UNIT V: Offences relating to Documents and Reputation: Offences relating to Documents and Property Marks: Sections 335–350 of BNS, 2023. Criminal Intimidation and Defamation: Criminal Intimidation; Insult; Annoyance; Sections 351–355 of BNS, 2023. Defamation under Section 356 of BNS, 2023. Breach of Contract: Breach of Contracts to attend on and supply wants of helpless persons; Section 357 of BNS, 2023
Course Content.UNIT II: Public Tranquillity and Public Servants: Offences relating to Currency and Government Stamps: Offences relating to Coin; Currency Notes; Bank Notes; Government Stamps; Sections 178–188 of BNS, 2023. Offences against Public Tranquillity: Sections 189–197 of BNS, 2023. Offences by or relating to Public Servants: Sections 198–205 of BNS, 2023
Course Content.UNIT IV: Offences against Religion and Property: Offences relating to Religion: Sections 298–302 of BNS, 2023. Offences against Property: Sections 303–334 of BNS, 2023; Theft; Robbery; Dacoity; Criminal Misappropriation of Property; Criminal Breach of Trust; Receiving Stolen Property; Cheating; Fraudulent Deeds and Disposition of Property; Mischief; Criminal Trespass
Course Content.UNIT III: Public Justice and Public Morality: Contempt of Lawful Authority: Sections 206–226 of BNS, 2023. False Evidence and Public Justice: False Evidence; Offences against Public Justice; Sections 227–269 of BNS, 2023. Public Health, Safety and Morality: Offences affecting Public Health; Public Safety; Public Convenience; Decency and Morals; Sections 270–297 of BNS, 2023

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to offences against the State, public tranquility and public justice under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. CO2: To examine offences relating to currency, public servants, religion and public order under criminal law. CO3: To analyze offences against property and offences affecting public morality and administration of justice. CO4: To understand criminal liability relating to documents, defamation, intimidation and public offences under BNS, 2023. CO5: To familiarize students with comparative developments between IPC, 1860 and BNS, 2023 through judicial interpretation and modern criminal jurisprudence.

syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts and principles relating to offences against the State and public order under BNS, 2023. CO4: To understand standing orders, disciplinary proceedings and principles of natural justice in industries. Course Content.UNIT I: General Principles of Transfer of Property: Meaning and Concept of Property; Kinds of Property; Transfer of Property; Transferable and Non-transferable Property; Who can Transfer; Operation of Transfer; Modes of Transfer; Conditional Transfer; Void and Unlawful Conditions; Condition Precedent and Condition Subsequent; Vested Interest; Contingent Interest; Transfer to Unborn Persons

CO2: To explain the doctrines relating to transfer of property and equitable principles. CO3: To develop understanding of sale, mortgage, lease and actionable claims. CO4: To familiarize students with easements, gifts and testamentary succession. CO5: To enable students to analyze legal rights and liabilities arising out of property transactions.

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Jurisprudence: Meaning and Definition of Jurisprudence; General Jurisprudence; Particular Jurisprudence; Elements of Ancient Indian Jurisprudence; Schools of Jurisprudence; Analytical School; Historical School; Philosophical School; Sociological School; Theories of Law; Meaning and Definition of Law; Nature and Functions of Law; Purpose of Law; Classification of Law; Equity, Law and Justice; Theory of Sovereignty

Course Content.VIVA–VOCE: The Viva-Voce Board shall consist of: Principal/Teacher concerned; University Representative appointed by Controller of Examinations in consultation with Chairman, BOS in Law; Advocate with 10 years standing at the Bar. The proceedings of Viva-Voce shall be recorded.
Course Content.PRACTICAL EXERCISES: (a) Simulation Proceedings – 20 Marks: Students shall participate in five simulation proceedings relating to: Arbitration; Conciliation; Mediation; Negotiation. Each simulation proceeding shall carry 4 marks. (b) Observation and Record – 10 Marks: Students shall: Attend Lok Adalats; Observe Family Courts; Observe Tribunals; Observe other ADR Systems. Students shall maintain a diary/record of observations. The record shall be evaluated by the teacher concerned.

Course Content.Unit-I: Historical and Constitutional Perspective of Women’s Rights: Historical background and status of women in ancient India; Constitutional provisions relating to women and gender justice; Fundamental Rights and women; Directive Principles of State Policy and Fundamental Duties relating to women; Equal right of women to worship

syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the structure, principles and salient features of Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023. Kelkar – Criminal Procedure; Ratanlal & Dhirajlal – Code of Criminal Procedure; S.N. Misra – Code of Criminal Procedure; M.P. Tandon – Criminal Procedure Code; Shoorvir Tyagi – Criminal Procedure Code; K. Thakker – Criminal Procedure Code; Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015; Probation of Offenders Act, 1958
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Hussainara Khatoon v State of Bihar; DK Basu v State of West Bengal; Joginder Kumar v State of Uttar Pradesh; Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar; Selvi v State of Karnataka; State of Haryana v Bhajan Lal; Sunil Batra v Delhi Administration; Sheela Barse v Union of India; Pratap Singh v State of Jharkhand; Zahira Habibullah Sheikh v State of Gujarat
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the framework, objectives and procedural principles of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Banking Law: 1. History of the Banking Regulation Act; 2. Salient Features of the Banking Regulation Act; 3. Banking Business; 4. Importance of Banking in Modern Times; 5. Different Kinds of Banking; 6. Impact of Information Technology on Banking
Course Content.UNIT V: Banker’s Securities and Recovery of Loans: 1. Banker’s Lien; 2. Set Off; 3. Advances; 4. Pledge; 5. Land as Security; 6. Stocks as Security; 7. Shares as Security; 8. Life Policies as Security; 9. Documents of Title to Goods; 10. Bank Guarantees; 11. Letters of Credit; 12. Recovery of Bank Loans; 13. SARFAESI Act, 2002; 14. Jurisdiction of Debt Recovery Tribunal; 15. Powers of Debt Recovery Tribunal

Trustee and Beneficiary Relationship; 5. Principal and Agent Relationship; 6. Bailor and Bailee Relationship; 7. Guarantor Relationship

Rights of Paying Banker; 6. Obligations of Paying Banker; 7. Rights of Collecting Banker; 8. Obligations of Collecting Banker
Course Content.UNIT III: Negotiable Instruments: 1. Cheques; 2. Crossed Cheques; 3. Account Payee Cheques; 4. Banker’s Drafts; 5. Dividend Warrants; 6. Negotiable Instruments; 7. Deemed Negotiable Instruments; 8. Salient Features of the Negotiable Instruments Act; 9. The Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2018

CO2: To analyze the kinds of legal relationships that exits between the bankers and customers. CO3: To examine the law relating to negotiable instruments in India. CO4: To familiarize students with the rights, duties, and statutory protections of paying and collecting bankers. CO5: To understand about the banking securities, recovery mechanisms, and legal remedies relating to bank loans.

CO3: Examine the legal principles governing negotiable instruments and banking transactions. CO4: Assess the rights, obligations, and statutory protections of paying and collecting bankers under Negotiable instruments act. Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Alternate Dispute Resolution: Alternate Dispute Resolution; Characteristics of ADR; Advantages and Disadvantages of ADR; Unilateral Processes; Bilateral Processes; Triadic (Third Party) Intervention; ADR Techniques and Processes; Negotiation; Conciliation; Mediation; Arbitration; Distinction between Arbitration, Conciliation and Negotiation; ADR under Different Laws in India
Course Content.UNIT II: Arbitration and Conciliation: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996; Historical Background and Objectives; Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act, 2015; Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act, 2019; Definitions of Arbitration, Arbitrator and Arbitration Agreement; Appointment and Termination of Arbitrator; Proceedings before Arbitral Tribunal; Termination of Proceedings; Arbitral Award; Setting Aside of Arbitral Award; Finality and Enforcement of Award; Appeals; Conciliation; Appointment, Powers and Functions of Conciliator; Procedure for Conciliation; Settlement through Conciliation; Arbitration Council of India (ACI); International Commercial Arbitration; UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration, 1985; Geneva Convention, 1927; New York Convention, 1958; Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Awards; UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Mediation, 2018; Singapore Convention on Mediation, 2019; Online Dispute Resolution (ODR)
Course Content.UNIT III: Other ADR Mechanisms: Tribunals; Lokpal and Lokayukta; Lok Adalats; Family Courts; Commercial Courts; Section 89 CPC; Order X Rules 1A, 1B and 1C CPC; ADR and Mediation Rules; Pre-Litigation Mediation in India
Course Content.VIVA–VOCE: Viva-voce examination shall be conducted on: ADR principles, Simulation exercises, Practical observations, Record submissions
Course Content.PRACTICAL EXERCISES: A. Simulation Proceedings (20 Marks): Students shall participate in five simulation proceedings relating to: Arbitration, Conciliation, Mediation, Negotiation. Each simulation proceeding shall carry 4 marks.Total: 5 × 4 = 20 Marks. B. Record Submission and Observation (10 Marks): Students shall: Attend Lok Adalats, Family Courts, Tribunals and ADR proceedings; Observe practical functioning of ADR mechanisms; Maintain a certified observation diary/record. The submitted record shall be evaluated for 10 marks.

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to concepts, techniques and significance of Alternate Dispute Resolution systems. CO2: To examine arbitration, conciliation, mediation and negotiation under Indian and international legal frameworks. CO3: To analyze statutory provisions governing arbitration and conciliation under Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. CO4: To develop practical skills relating to negotiation, mediation and arbitration proceedings. CO5: To familiarize students with institutional ADR mechanisms and emerging trends such as Online Dispute Resolution.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: O.P. Tiwari – Arbitration and Conciliation Act; Johar’s Commentary on Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996; S.C. Tripathi – Arbitration, Conciliation and ADR; Avtar Singh – Arbitration and Conciliation; P.C. Rao – Alternate Dispute Resolution; S.D. Singh – Alternate Dispute Resolution; Sriram Panchu – Mediation: Practice and Law; Anirban Chakraborty – Law and Practice of ADR in India; Madhusudan Saharay – Textbook on Arbitration and ADR; Margaret L. Moses – Principles and Practice of International Commercial Arbitration; Harsh Sethi & Arpan Kr Gupta – International Commercial Arbitration and Indian Perspective
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Booz Allen and Hamilton Inc v SBI Home Finance Ltd; Bharat Aluminium Co v Kaiser Aluminium Technical Services Inc; ONGC Ltd v Saw Pipes Ltd; Venture Global Engineering v Satyam Computer Services Ltd; Afcons Infrastructure Ltd v Cherian Varkey Construction Co Pvt Ltd; Salem Advocate Bar Association v Union of India; K.K. Modi v K.N. Modi; M.R. Engineers and Contractors Pvt Ltd v Som Datt Builders Ltd; Vidya Drolia v Durga Trading Corporation; Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v HSCC (India) Ltd
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts, objectives and importance of Alternate Dispute Resolution mechanisms. CO2: Analyze legal provisions governing arbitration, conciliation and mediation under Indian law. CO3: Examine institutional ADR mechanisms and international commercial arbitration frameworks. CO4: Apply ADR techniques in negotiation, mediation and arbitration simulation proceedings. CO5: Evaluate effectiveness of ADR systems in dispute resolution and access to justice.

syllabus.Course Title: PROFESSIONAL ETHICS AND PROFESSIONAL ACCOUNTING SYSTEM

Course Content.UNIT I: Legal Profession and Advocacy: Development of Legal Profession in India; Advocates Act, 1961; Right to Practice; Right or Privilege Debate; Article 19(1)(g) and Legal Profession; Enrolment and Practice; Regulations Governing Enrolment; Latest Bar Council of India Rules; Practice of Law; All India Bar Examination (AIBE); Advocates and Solicitors’ Firms; Elements of Advocacy
Course Content.UNIT II: Professional Ethics and Duties of Advocates: Seven Lamps of Advocacy; Duties of Advocates towards Public; Duties towards Clients; Duties towards Court; Duties towards Other Advocates; Legal Aid; Bar Council of India Code of Ethics
Course Content.UNIT IV: Professional Accounting and Bench-Bar Relations: Professional Accounting; Accountancy for Lawyers; Nature and Functions of Accounting; Important Branches of Accounting; Accounting and Law; Bench-Bar Relations
Course Content.UNIT III: Professional Misconduct and Disciplinary Proceedings: Disciplinary Proceedings; Professional Misconduct; Disqualifications; Functions of Bar Council of India; Functions of State Bar Councils; Disciplinary Committees; Powers and Functions of Disciplinary Committees; Removal from Rolls of Advocates
Course Content.RECORD WORK: Each student shall prepare a record containing: 50 selected opinions of Disciplinary Committees of Bar Councils; 10 major judgments of the Supreme Court of India relating to Professional Ethics. The record shall be evaluated for 30 marks by the teacher concerned.
Course Content.VIVA–VOCE: Viva-voce examination shall be conducted on: Professional ethics, Disciplinary proceedings, Advocacy standards, Accountancy for lawyers, Record submissions

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the development, regulation and ethical standards of legal profession in India. CO2: To examine professional duties, advocacy ethics and standards prescribed under the Advocates Act and Bar Council Rules. CO3: To analyze disciplinary mechanisms and professional misconduct proceedings relating to advocates. CO4: To understand principles of professional accounting and bench-bar relations in legal practice. CO5: To develop ethical, professional and practical skills necessary for responsible legal practice.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Sirohi – Professional Ethics; G.B. Reddy – Practical Advocacy of Law; S.R. Myneni – Professional Ethics, Accountancy for Lawyers and Bench-Bar Relations; S.P. Gupta – Professional Ethics, Accountancy for Lawyers and Bench-Bar Relations; Kailash Rai – Professional Ethics, Accountancy for Lawyers and Bench-Bar Relations; Selected Judgments on Professional Ethics (2 Volumes), Bar Council of India Trust; Advocates Act, 1961; Bar Council of India Rules
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Bar Council of Maharashtra v M.V. Dabholkar; V.C. Rangadurai v D. Gopalan; P.D. Khandekar v Bar Council of Maharashtra; R.K. Anand v Delhi High Court; Ex-Capt. Harish Uppal v Union of India; O.P. Sharma v High Court of Punjab and Haryana; In Re Vinay Chandra Mishra; Supreme Court Bar Association v Union of India; Mahipal Singh Rana v State of Uttar Pradesh; T.A. Kathiru Kunju v Jacob Mathai
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the development, regulation and ethical framework of legal profession in India. CO2: Analyze duties and responsibilities of advocates towards clients, courts and society. CO3: Examine disciplinary proceedings and professional misconduct under Advocates Act and BCI Rules. CO4: Apply principles of professional ethics, advocacy and accounting in legal practice. CO5: Evaluate professional standards, ethical obligations and bench-bar relationships in administration of justice.

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Taxation Law: Constitutional Basis of Taxation; Article 265 of Constitution of India; Basic Concepts of Income Tax; Outlines of Income Tax Law; Definition of Income; Agricultural Income under Income Tax Act; Residential Status; Previous Year; Assessment Year; Computation of Income
Course Content.UNIT V: Goods and Services Tax – II: Registration under GST; Persons liable for Registration; Persons not liable for Registration; Procedure for Registration; Returns under GST; Furnishing of Outward and Inward Supplies; Payment of Tax, Interest and Penalty; Tax Deducted at Source; Collection of Tax at Source; Demand and Recovery; Advance Ruling; Appeals and Revision; Appellate Authority under GST; Revisional Authority; Constitution of Appellate Tribunal; Offences and Penalties under GST
Course Content.UNIT II: Heads of Income and Computation: Heads of Income; Income from Salary; Income from House Property; Profits and Gains from Business or Profession; Capital Gains; Income from Other Sources; Taxation Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019
Course Content.UNIT IV: Goods and Services Tax – I: GST Act, 2017; Introduction and Background of GST; Basic Concepts of GST; Salient Features of GST Act; Kinds of GST; CGST; SGST; IGST; Administration Officers under GST Act; Levy and Collection of Tax; Scope of Supply; Tax Liability on Composite and Mixed Supplies; Input Tax Credit; Eligibility and Conditions for Input Tax Credit
Course Content.UNIT III: Tax Procedure and Authorities: Permanent Account Number (PAN); Filing of Returns; Advance Tax; Deduction of Tax at Source (TDS); Double Tax Relief; Assessment Procedures; Penalties; Prosecution under Tax Laws; Appeals and Grievances; Tax Authorities and their Functions

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to constitutional principles and legal framework governing taxation laws in India. CO2: To examine concepts and computation of income under Income Tax Law. CO3: To analyze assessment procedures, tax authorities and remedies under taxation laws. CO4: To understand the structure, administration and operation of Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India. CO5: To familiarize students with tax compliance, procedural requirements and dispute resolution mechanisms under taxation laws.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: Vinod K. Singhania – Student Guide to Income Tax; Vinod K. Singhania – Direct Taxes Law and Practice; S.R. Myneni – Law of Taxation; Kailash Rai – Taxation Laws; Girish Ahuja – Systematic Approach to Income Tax; V.S. Datey – GST Ready Reckoner; GST Acts with Rules and Forms (Bare Act); GST – A Practical Approach; Sweta Jain – GST Law and Practice
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Commissioner of Income Tax v B.C. Srinivasa Setty; McDowell & Co Ltd v Commercial Tax Officer; Vodafone International Holdings BV v Union of India; Union of India v Mohit Minerals Pvt Ltd; Mafatlal Industries Ltd v Union of India; Kesoram Industries Ltd v State of West Bengal; Govind Saran Ganga Saran v Commissioner of Sales Tax; A.V. Fernandez v State of Kerala; State of West Bengal v Kesoram Industries Ltd; Union of India v VKC Footsteps India Pvt Ltd
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain constitutional principles and statutory framework governing taxation laws in India. CO2: Analyze provisions relating to computation of income and heads of income under Income Tax Law. CO3: Examine legal procedures relating to tax assessment, appeals, penalties and tax administration. CO4: Apply principles of GST law relating to registration, levy, input tax credit and returns. CO5: Evaluate taxation mechanisms, compliance systems and dispute resolution processes under Indian tax laws.

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Cyber Law and Jurisdiction: Concept of Information Technology; Cyber Space; Interface of Technology and Law; Jurisdiction in Cyber Space; Traditional Jurisdiction; Internet Jurisdiction; Indian Context of Cyber Jurisdiction; Enforcement Agencies; International Position on Internet Jurisdiction; Cases relating to Cyber Jurisdiction
Course Content.UNIT V: Cyber Crimes and Data Protection: Meaning of Cyber Crimes; Kinds of Cyber Crimes; Cyber Crimes under BNS, BNSS and BSA, 2023; Cyber Crimes under Information Technology Act, 2000; Cyber Crimes under International Law; Hacking; Child Pornography; Cyber Stalking; Denial of Service Attack; Virus Dissemination; Software Piracy; Internet Relay Chat Crimes; Credit Card Fraud; Net Extortion; Phishing; Cyber Terrorism; Violation of Privacy on Internet; Data Protection and Privacy
Course Content.UNIT II: Information Technology Act, 2000: Information Technology Act, 2000; Aims and Objectives of the Act; Overview of the Act; Jurisdiction under IT Act; Electronic Governance; Legal Recognition of Electronic Records; Electronic Evidence; Digital Signature Certificates; Secure Electronic Records; Secure Digital Signatures; Duties of Subscribers; Certifying Authorities; Regulators under IT Act; Cyber Regulations Appellate Tribunal; Internet Service Providers and Liability; Powers of Police under IT Act; Impact of IT Act on other Laws
Course Content.UNIT IV: Cyber Law and Intellectual Property Rights: Copyright in Information Technology; Software Protection; Copyright versus Patent Debate; Authorship and Assignment Issues; Copyright in Internet; Multimedia and Copyright Issues; Software Piracy; Patents in Information Technology; European Position on Computer Related Patents; U.S. Position on Computer Related Patents; Indian Position on Computer Related Patents; Trademarks in Internet; Domain Name Registration; Domain Name Disputes and WIPO; Database Protection; Position in USA, EU and India
Course Content.UNIT III: E-Commerce and Electronic Contracts: E-Commerce; UNCITRAL Model Law; Legal Aspects of E-Commerce; Digital Signatures; Technical and Legal Issues; Trends and Prospects of E-Commerce; E-Taxation; E-Banking; Online Publishing; Online Credit Card Payments; Employment Contracts; Contractor Agreements; Sales Agreements; Re-Seller and Distributor Agreements; Non-Disclosure Agreements; Shrink Wrap Contracts; Source Code Agreements; Escrow Agreements

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the concepts of cyber space, information technology and cyber jurisdiction. CO2: To examine the legal framework governing electronic governance and cyber regulations under Information Technology Act, 2000. CO3: To analyze legal issues relating to e-commerce, electronic contracts and digital transactions. CO4: To understand intellectual property issues and cybercrimes arising in digital environment. CO5: To familiarize students with cyber security, privacy, data protection and emerging challenges in cyber law.

James – The Internet: A User’s Guide; Chris Reed – Internet Law: Text and Materials; Vakul Sharma – Handbook of Cyber Laws; S.V. Joga Rao – Computer Contracts and IT Laws; T. Ramappa – Legal Issues in Electronic Commerce; Indian Law Institute – Legal Dimensions of Cyber Space; Pankaj Jain & Sangeet Rai Pandey – Copyright and Trademark Laws relating to Computers; Farouq Ahmed – Cyber Law in India; S.V. Joga Rao – Law of Cyber Crimes and Information Technology Law
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Shreya Singhal v Union of India; Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India; State of Tamil Nadu v Suhas Katti; Avnish Bajaj v State (Bazee.com Case); Yahoo Inc v Akash Arora; Google India Pvt Ltd v Visaka Industries; Anvar P.V. v P.K. Basheer; Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal; Trimex International FZE Ltd v Vedanta Aluminium Ltd; People's Union for Civil Liberties v Union of India
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the concepts, scope and legal framework of Information Technology Law. CO2: Analyze provisions of Information Technology Act, 2000 and electronic governance mechanisms. CO3: Examine legal issues relating to e-commerce, cyber jurisdiction and electronic contracts. CO4: Apply legal principles relating to cybercrimes, digital evidence and intellectual property in cyberspace. CO5: Evaluate challenges relating to cyber security, privacy and data protection in the digital era.

Course Content.UNIT I: Historical and Constitutional Perspective of Women’s Rights: Historical Background and Status of Women in Ancient India; Constitutional Provisions relating to Women; Gender Justice under Indian Constitution; Fundamental Rights relating to Women; Directive Principles of State Policy; Fundamental Duties; Equal Right of Women to Worship
Course Content.UNIT V: Women under Labour Laws and International Law: Position of Women under Maternity Benefit Act; Position of Women under Factories Act; Position of Women under Labour and Industrial Laws; Women under Labour Codes; Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW); International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights; International Covenant on Social, Cultural and Economic Rights
Course Content.UNIT II: Women under Personal Laws and Family Laws: Marriage Laws relating to Women; Divorce Laws relating to Women; Succession Laws relating to Women; Maintenance under Personal Laws; Special Marriage Act; Maintenance under Criminal Procedure Code; NRI Marriages; Live-in Relationships; Uniform Civil Code and Gender Justice; Personal Laws (Amendment) Act, 2019
Course Content.UNIT IV: Socio-Legal Protection of Women: Socio-Legal Position of Women; Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961; Medical Termination of Pregnancy Act; Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques and Sex Selection Laws; Immoral Trafficking Laws; Domestic Violence Laws; Sexual Harassment at Workplace; Honour Killings
Course Content.UNIT III: Criminal Law Protection for Women: Special Provisions relating to Women under BSA, 2023; Offences against Women under BNS, 2023; Outraging Modesty of Women; Acid Attacks; Sexual Harassment; Rape; Bigamy; Mock and Fraudulent Marriages; Adultery and its Decriminalization; Causing Miscarriage; Insulting Women; Impact of New Criminal Laws, 2023

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the historical and constitutional development of women’s rights in India. CO2: To examine personal laws and statutory protections relating to marriage, maintenance and succession concerning women. CO3: To analyze criminal laws and legal protections relating to offences against women under new criminal laws. CO4: To understand socio-legal issues affecting women including domestic violence, workplace harassment and reproductive rights. CO5: To familiarize students with international legal instruments and labour protections relating to women’s rights and gender justice.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: S.P. Sathe – Towards Gender Justice; Vijay Sharma – Protection to Women in Matrimonial Home; Sarojini Saxena – Femijuris (Law relating to Women in India); Archana Parashar – Women and Social Reform; Paras Diwan – Dowry and Protection to Married Women; Mary Wollstonecraft – A Vindication of the Rights of Women; G.B. Reddy – Women and Law; Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961; Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005; Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Vishaka v State of Rajasthan; Shayara Bano v Union of India; Joseph Shine v Union of India; Independent Thought v Union of India; Lata Singh v State of Uttar Pradesh; Suchita Srivastava v Chandigarh Administration; Danial Latifi v Union of India; Mary Roy v State of Kerala; Githa Hariharan v Reserve Bank of India; Indian Young Lawyers Association v State of Kerala
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the constitutional and legal framework relating to women’s rights in India. CO2: Analyze personal laws, maintenance laws and gender justice mechanisms affecting women. CO3: Examine criminal law provisions and socio-legal protections relating to offences against women. CO4: Apply legal principles relating to domestic violence, workplace harassment and reproductive rights. CO5: Evaluate national and international legal mechanisms promoting gender equality and protection of women’s rights.

Course Content.UNIT I: Introduction to Human Rights: Meaning and Definition of Human Rights; Evolution of Human Rights; Human Rights and Domestic Jurisdiction; Classification of Human Rights; Third World Perspectives of Human Rights
Course Content.UNIT V: Human Rights Protection in India: Human Rights Protection in India; Protection of Human Rights Act; National Human Rights Commission (NHRC); State Human Rights Commissions; Human Rights Courts in Districts; Functions and Powers of Human Rights Institutions
Course Content.UNIT II: United Nations and Human Rights: Human Rights under United Nations Charter; U.N. Commission on Human Rights; Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR); International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (ICCPR); International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR)
Course Content.UNIT IV: International Human Rights Conventions: Genocide Convention; Convention against Torture; Convention on Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW); Child Rights Convention; Convention on Statelessness; Convention against Slavery; Convention on Refugees; International Conference on Human Rights, 1968; World Conference on Human Rights, 1993
Course Content.UNIT III: Regional Human Rights Systems: Regional Conventions on Human Rights; European Convention on Human Rights; American Convention on Human Rights; African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights (Banjul Charter)

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to the concept, evolution and classification of human rights. CO2: To examine international human rights instruments and United Nations human rights framework. CO3: To analyze regional and international conventions relating to protection of human rights. CO4: To understand institutional mechanisms for protection and enforcement of human rights in India and internationally. CO5: To familiarize students with contemporary human rights issues and the role of international organizations and national institutions.
syllabus.Suggested Readings: P.R. Gandhi (Ed.) – Blackstone’s International Human Rights Documents; Richard B. Lillich & Frank C. Newman – International Human Rights: Problems of Law and Policy; Frederick Quinn – Human Rights and You; T.S. Batra – Human Rights: A Critique; Dr. U. Chandra – Human Rights; Universal Declaration of Human Rights, 1948; Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights; International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
syllabus.Suggested Case Laws: Maneka Gandhi v Union of India; Vishaka v State of Rajasthan; D.K. Basu v State of West Bengal; Olga Tellis v Bombay Municipal Corporation; Francis Coralie Mullin v Administrator, Union Territory of Delhi; People's Union for Civil Liberties v Union of India; National Human Rights Commission v State of Arunachal Pradesh; Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala; ADM Jabalpur v Shivkant Shukla; Bandhua Mukti Morcha v Union of India
syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain the meaning, nature and evolution of human rights at national and international levels. CO2: Analyze international and regional human rights instruments and conventions. CO3: Examine legal mechanisms for protection and enforcement of human rights. CO4: Apply human rights principles to issues relating to discrimination, torture, refugees and vulnerable groups. CO5: Evaluate the role of international organizations and national institutions in promotion and protection of human rights.

Course Content.UNIT V: Writing Skills: Paragraph Writing; Formal Correspondence; Note Taking

Course Content.UNIT IV: Comprehension Skills: Reading Comprehension; Principles of Reading Comprehension; Practice of Reading Comprehension; Listening Comprehension
Course Content.UNIT III: Vocabulary and Legal Communication: Vocabulary Development; Communication Skills; Legal Terms; Idiomatic Expressions

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To develop grammatical competence and sentence construction skills among students. CO2: To enhance communication skills through vocabulary development and legal terminology. CO3: To improve reading, listening and comprehension abilities required for legal studies. CO4: To develop writing skills relating to paragraphs, correspondence and note-taking. CO5: To strengthen language proficiency necessary for legal communication and professional interaction.

syllabus.Course Learning Outcomes: CO1: Explain grammatical structures and sentence patterns in English language usage. CO2: Analyze sentence construction, transformations and common grammatical errors. CO3: Demonstrate effective use of vocabulary, legal terminology and communication skills. CO4: Apply reading, listening and comprehension techniques in academic and legal contexts. CO5: Develop effective writing skills for paragraphs, formal correspondence and note-making.

Gopalan v State of Madras; Donoghue v Stevenson; Vishaka v State of Rajasthan; Shreya Singhal v Union of India; Navtej Singh Johar v Union of India; Justice K.S. Puttaswamy v Union of India; Indra Sawhney v Union of India; Olga Tellis v Bombay Municipal Corporation

Course Content.UNIT I: Forms of Business Organization: Sole Proprietorship; Partnership; Cooperative Societies; Joint Stock Companies; Characteristics of Business Organizations; Strengths and Limitations of Business Organizations; Distinction between Partnership and Firm; Firm and Reconstituted Firm; Kinds of Partners; Formation of Joint Stock Company; Memorandum of Association; Articles of Association; Kinds of Companies; Difference between Private Company and Public Company
Course Content.UNIT V: Motivation, Leadership and Communication: Meaning and Process of Motivation; Elements of Motivation; Need Hierarchy Theory; Two Factor Theory; Theory X and Theory Y; Leadership; Difference between Leaders and Managers; Trait Theory of Leadership; Behavioural Theory of Leadership; Contingency Theory of Leadership; Decision Making; Steps in Decision Making; Types and Limitations of Decision Making; Communication; Elements of Communication; Types of Communication; Barriers to Communication; Overcoming Barriers to Communication

Course Content.UNIT IV: Organization Structure and Delegation: Nature and Significance of Organization Structure; Types of Organization Structure; Line and Staff Organization; Nature and Use of Authority; Authority vs Power; Sources of Power; Delegation of Authority; Barriers to Delegation; Centralization; Decentralization; Merits and Demerits of Centralization and Decentralization
Course Content.UNIT III: Planning and Management by Objectives: Nature of Planning; Types of Planning; Planning Premises; Steps in Comprehensive Planning; Contingency Planning; Limitations of Planning; Management by Objectives (MBO); MBO Process; Benefits of MBO; Problems of MBO; Factors Essential for MBO Process

syllabus.Course Objectives: CO1: To introduce students to various forms of business organizations and principles of management.
